candidates.official_title: Saint Laurence O'Toole's Church, Seville Place, Sherriff Street Lower, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
candidates.address: Seville Place / Sherriff Street Lower, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidates.architects: John B. Keane; steeple by John Bourke
candidates.description_summary: Freestanding cruciform limestone Gothic Revival Roman Catholic church with five-bay nave, gabled transepts, chancel, four-stage tower, broach spire, pointed-arch openings, geometric tracery and stained glass.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH says it served the growing dockworker community and remains a local landmark/social focal point. Appraisal says begun in 1844 by John B. Keane and completed in 1858 by John Bourke; this conflicts with the survey/date-range fields and is retained as an unresolved source-internal discrepancy.

candidates.official_title: Saint Laurence O'Toole School, Saint Laurence Place East, Sheriff Street Lower, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
candidates.address: Saint Laurence Place East / Sheriff Street Lower, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidates.description_summary: Attached multiple-bay two-storey limestone school range in church grounds, including boys' and girls' school ranges, connecting wings, pointed-arch and square-headed openings, limestone dressings and decorative roof features.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies the group as a local landmark with an important educational role and links it to Catholic education after Emancipation.

candidates.official_title: 49 Seville Place, Saint Laurence Place East, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
candidates.address: 49 Seville Place, Saint Laurence Place East, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidates.description_summary: Corner-sited attached three-bay three-storey presbytery over raised basement, with mixed garden-wall-bond red brick, granite quoins and dressings, varied sash windows and paired recessed porches.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH highlights its two principal elevations, Lombardic detailing, high-quality stonework and place in an ecclesiastical/educational cluster.

candidates.official_title: 47 Seville Place, Marion Terrace, Dublin 1, DUBLIN

candidates.description_summary: Terraced two-bay two-storey brown-brick house in Flemish bond, with M-profile slate roof, granite coping and plinth, gauged brick window heads, sash windows, moulded entrance surround, panelled door and wrought-iron railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies it as one of five well-proportioned houses in a terrace developed in the second half of the nineteenth century.
